request: 正常更新重启不再当异常报错，改成普通服务已更新请刷新页面提示
acceptance: Service instance changes show ordinary 服务已更新，请刷新页面 notice, with explicit refresh/dismiss and no automatic reload or incident.
Old AIDE-SERVICE-RESTARTED metadata does not appear as an error.
Real script errors, server panic and persistent unreachable service diagnostics remain unchanged.

requirements.summary: User explicitly requests ordinary refresh notice for service updates.

design.summary: Treat instance change as informational only; health probes cannot establish whether replacement was planned. Keep actual outage/panic diagnostics separate. Ignore legacy instance-change records in diagnostic reader without modifying other reports.

implementation.summary: Separate polite status notice with neutral border and refresh/dismiss actions; no incident code/ID/stack. Existing diagnostic notice takes priority, lock hides both. Bumped monitor resources in workbench and starmap.

verification.summary: PASS: crash-monitor regression including legacy records, explicit-only reload, dismiss, lock, subsequent replacement and diagnostic priority. All 104 quick checks passed after rerun with local socket permission. Source build/vet/startup passed. Browser component with real monitor/CSS and simulated health instance verified notice/close. Running localhost9999 serves byte-identical new JS/CSS and health ok.

documentation.summary: Recorded scope, test evidence and limitations in this task.

cleanup.summary: Reviewed scoped diff, closed component tab and stopped owned fixture server. User Safari tabs retained.

release.summary: Local source candidate updated only; no commit/push/version/tag/Release requested in this turn.

rollback: Restore scoped monitor behavior, styles, locale additions and cache versions; keep unrelated work.
handoff: Local9999 healthy with new monitor. Existing open pages retain old script until refreshed once; cannot replace already-loaded diagnostics without page refresh.
verification_limits: Browser proof uses a simulated health response with actual monitor and CSS; no deliberate extra restart of real service for notice timing.
Service replacement alone does not prove a normal update or a crash; real persistent failure and server panic remain diagnostic events.
